Also shout out to the hilariously invader named "SirCheekClaps" that I killed before I fought the final boss XD

Still as great as dark souls 1, but as a remaster it's lacking, it added nothing, the difference in graphics is similar to a mod download, however, the frames are much smoother and almost always stay at 60fps. Having the summoning system work is also a plus, but matchmaking is probably the worst part of the game, since it relies on weapons instead of stats, someone could just not pick up any weapons and then invade using high level magic. TL:DR a good game, and worth buying instead of the original, but if you already have played the original, you'll find it disappointing, or maybe you'll enjoy it, it is still dark souls.

For every time I get annoyed / tired of DS2 or DS3, I replay this game 1-3 times.
I feel like a little kid with a big lollipop and a propeller hat when I play this game.

I never use anything but a melee weapon and maybe some armor in these games. And everyone knows summons are for twinks. ...But what if you summon a twink? There was a summon stone for a player named MrTrans... who could possibly resist that? Ofc I summoned MrTrans to see his decepticon skills... Unfortunately, MrTrans seems to be no GDQ speedrunner, as he got almost oneshot by Smough. RIP MrTrans.
Also, don't 100% this game, it's a nightmare. Otherwise, very fun.

I have been playing souls games for years, starting on ds1 on the xbox360 and they have been a constant source of fun constantly, this is a great entry point for newcomers as its not only the start of the story its tutorial level is the best at teaching you how to play while still being short (like all the games) its not too long of a game if you know what youre doing, but its new game plus adds a reason to keep playing after beating it, I have 100%d this game 3 times now and own it on every console its available on.
With this version including the dlc you also get an additional decently sized chunk of gameplay.
at first i thought the game is super hard and felt impossible. but then i keep playing and get better, thanks to this game now i keep following fromsoftware games. they make great games :)

This game was my first inspiration for playing other HQ combat games. When i saw this game on steam I thought next: ''This. Is. Epic'' (And looks good, too) And when i noticed that they will make a remaster I was so happy and excited. And now, here i am- loving my childhood game hard core! Btw i recommend it for all the players who haven't played this game. Truly! Trust me! This game has big potential of blowing up your mind. The game mechanics are moch more visual and realistic, and the graphics are beautiful. Loving your work, Miasaki, keep up the good game making.

DS1 definitely has a level of clunk considering how old it is, but is definitely genre defining considering how it started the legendary souls series. I do think DS1's boss designs are extremely well made and slower than other dark souls games which makes them unique. The level design in this game is immaculate, some of which being very iconic within soulsborne. Personally my favourite dark souls game, slightly edging DS3. I highly reccomend a download if you are thinking about it, but pick up a controller first.

Hands down the sleekest Dark Souls game. it is IMO the best and most concrete environmental narrative experience in any game in the soulsborne franchise (aside from Bloodborne). This game also most notably has an astonishing interconnected world design where memory, verticality and architecture are your navigation tools. It's my favorite DS game to revisit.
Don't be afraid to google stuff this game has absolutely no tutorial or info on the mechanics but once you get it it's peak.

It's a great game, the bosses are amazing, but some of the areas are a massive pain to get through, and some of the bosses are far too far away from bonfires.

You need a serious amount of patience for this game.

Diğer Souls oyunlarını bitirdikten sonra başladım, bu yüzden bonfire arası mesafeler ve sınırlı ışınlanma başlarda biraz zorlasa da, atmosferi bana çok daha nostaljik ve güzel geldi. Bölüm tasarımları etkileyici, boss savaşları (2 istisna dışında) dengeliydi; en sevdiğim bosslar açık ara Knight Artorias ve Great Grey Wolf Sif oldu. Hikayeleri de ayrı bir keyif. Tekrar oynanabilirliği sınırlı gibi görünebilir(Sıkılabilirsiniz), ama ben dört kez bitirdim ve her seferinde keyif aldım. Souls hayranlarına kesinlikle tavsiye ederim.

Holy shit, what a game. The enviroment is stunning, the level design is absolutely incredible in all respects. The satisfaction of unlocking a new shortcut never gets old, its a massive relief and gives the player a small reassurance of safety. The combat was pretty fun, in my opinion its not as good as Dark Souls 3 or Elden Ring but if we are looking purely at the time this is leagues above other games. I had some gripes with some boss hitboxes, the main ones were the Half Dragon and really any dragon but thats typical for souls games. Highly recommend you play through, the first hour is not going to be all that fun considering you kind of have to bruteforce to learn the mechanics and how to navigate the world, but after that it is literally all enjoyment.

I love this game , even though I get my butt handed to me it never gets old. I cant explain how mad this game makes me but I cant stop playing because of its lore and lovable bosses and characters. 10/10

It is crazy how this game is still fun asf. I completed the entirety of it with 100% achievements and even tho this is my first time playing this old ass game i still felt right at home. It just shows you the dedication and love that fromsoft has always put into their games
This game, as well as every other game in the Dark Souls series, is a masterpiece. I think anyone that plays games should play at least one Dark Souls game in their life.

Masterpiece. One of the best games I have ever played. The story and the world building to support it are phenomenal. The atmosphere is amazing and so is the soundtrack. Definitely an all timer. The way the world all fits together and you travel all around seamlessly is awesome. Really felt like i was lost in this fantasy world and truly a part of it. 10/10

when I first played dark souls I was discouraged with how hard it was. I stopped playing for months after my first day or 2 of trying to progress. I picked it up later though because I do enjoy RPG's and I was still very intrigued by the story. When I came back I truly realized how much of a masterpiece this game is. Tough but fair. No spoonfeeding or hand holding. Great sense of accomplishment the first time you defeat a boss, or get through a rough area. The level design is out of this world, the gameplay and lore significance being tied together so well is also just amazing. Even has good music and interesting characters. Tons of replay value as some things are so well hidden it may take multiple play throughs. Plus the variety in character builds adds something as well. This game made me in to a lifelong FromSoftware and Miyazaki fan.

It's Dark Souls, and it's remastered. If you expected gameplay changes or redone areas, that is not what they promised. That's 100% on you.

It runs smooth at 60fps, no frame dips in blighttown, much better looking visuals (they removed that gross slimy texture every wall had in the OG)

The networking is massively improved too, had no issues getting into PvP or co-op with a friend.

It's a great remaster of a great game.

My best hours with this were spent cautiously exploring new areas and sparring with difficult bosses (the DLC was especially great for this); my worst were spent grinding for resources and not knowing where or how to proceed. I still appreciated its lack of straightforwardness most of the time, considering in comparison how insistent many modern games are to restrict your ability to venture off the beaten path and make big mistakes. I don't think its approach is ideal, though; there's very little guidance on how to spec a character, and the lack of a respec utility had me questioning in the late-game whether I was dead-ending myself with my DEX build. Still, I was able to make it through, which should prepare me well for the next time I visit its world.

Maybe I should have read the reviews before I paid money for this game. I am left hand and have always used the arrow keys for movement, not the wasd keys. The fact that this game will not let me remap key to fit my playstyle is beyond madding. Do not buy this game if you do not use the basic right handed layout because you will not be able to change them. This with others being able to just show up when they feel like it to mess around with your game play makes it basiclly unplayable. Stay far away.

I always thought I would hate Dark Souls games, but this is incredibly fun. It's just hard enough that when you are about to rage quit you get passed the part you were stuck on and it's a magical moment. You will die a lot, but it's part of the game. Highly recommended.

I love Dark Souls. It's in my Top 10 and frankly I'm not sure what people wanted from the Remastered when I read some reviews here. Sure I wouldn't buy it for the full price (and I didn't) but wait till it's on sale and there's nothing really wrong here!

The game features improved textures, 60fps, 144p and 144hz compatibility, and a small patch of quality of life changes. This is all I expected and it's all I got. It's still Dark Souls and I love it.

The retail price is too steep; so if you own OG Dark Souls wait till a sale because this won't offer you anything different other than a better looking experience. I have 150 hours on OG and almost 50 hours on remastered and I'm still loving it.

The Dark Souls Trilogy is a series of games that hold a special place in my heart. Although I played them out of order, I can certainly see why this one seems to be one of the favorites of the community. The sheer amount of content you get in this game is unmatched with anything you'll buy nowadays. Dark Souls: Remastered teaches perseverance, which is something I'd consider to be a virtue. Despite its convoluted lore, the game ignites a passion and interest in me that not many other games manage to do. So sit back, grab a snack, and get ready for a game that will teach you a lot about the importance of perseverance and the rewards that virtue reaps.

A little overpriced ($39.99) vs the older "Prepare to Die Edition" ($4.99 at it's lowest), but this is the only version you can purchase on Steam anymore. Also, that is still cheaper (and a better game) than most AAA games being released.

The Improved graphics/FPS are noticeable. Blighttown has smooth FPS.

If you are a Souls fan and have never played Dark Souls 1 before, what are you waiting for?!

My absolute favorite game I have ever played and for several great reasons. From software has a devolped a well written story, and there is tons of lore to go off of. It has fantastic gameplay including but not limited to, great boss fights, loads of weapons, spells, and armor to cultivate your ideal builds, endless replayability I've been playing for years and i still enjoy playing it. ∞/10 would recommend

Don't know why people keep telling DarkSouls very complex. It's not very hard. The only thing that makes Dark Souls "DARK SOULS" is, it has no enemy lv. grade system. That means if you are on lv.2/3 in some areas you can encounter lv.20+ enemies which will eventually lead to death only by their one hit.
The only thing that requires to play Dark Souls is patience.
"WAIT TILL YOU GET SOME DECENT GEAR AND WEAPONS THEN YOU CAN ONE HIT KILL ALMOST ANY ENEMY INCLUDING SKELETONS"
until then just avoid unnecessary fights.

I decided when I started getting really into Elden Ring that I wanted to not only 100% that game, but also the rest of the souls games. So when I finally finished all the achievements in Elden Ring, I redownloaded this game. It wasn't the first time I played it, but now that I had more experience with the type of gameplay thanks to Elden Ring, I was more confident in my abilities. But I was not ready for the difference in playstyle I would have to adapt to. In Elden Ring I used dual great axes. But here I ended up using the Zweihander. The game was far more challenging than Elden Ring, even if it didn't take as long to 100%. I enjoyed the challenge and sense of humility this game forces on you, and it's helped me appreciate more difficult games. Thank you FromSoftware for making such a great game! Edit: Hours later, I have also beaten the bosses in the DLC.

One of the absolute most fulfilling games in existence. You have to earn everything, but it feels so good when you do. Still super-fun and playable. It's a game I go back to when I am bored with more current gameplay.

Dark Souls Remastered is a true delight for both fans of the original and newcomers. The graphics are significantly improved, making the world of Lordran even more impressive and detailed with updated textures and lighting. Each area looks more vibrant and realistic, with added details making exploration even more captivating.

The gameplay remains just as challenging and rewarding, preserving the unique atmosphere of the game. The game offers more stable online functionalities, enhancing both cooperative and competitive play. Boss fights and exploration of different areas are as tense as ever, requiring strategic thinking and patience.

The controls are smoother and more responsive, making combat and exploration more enjoyable. Animations are more refined, and the controls are more precise, facilitating battles with enemies and navigation through the complex world of the game.

The soundtrack and sound effects are still atmospheric and contribute to the tension and epic feel of the game. The musical compositions create a unique mood in each area, while the sound effects further enhance the sense of danger and mystery.

"Dark Souls Remastered" is a must-play for anyone who loves intense and strategic RPG games. The game manages to retain the spirit of the original while providing a modernized and improved experience for both new and old fans.

One of the most popular games, from what I've been hearing. Saw some game play of it and was never intrigued. I read the manga Berserk, as well as watched the anime. When I found out Dark Souls was inspired off the manga, I had to give it a try. The small references to Berserk are there, but this game is on a level of its own. The progression throughout the game is satisfying. Even though there are times where you are setback and it can send you into a tilt. The fact that it's easy enough to recover souls, (which is the only setback from death, minus having to kill everyone all over again). The game is addicting and is always dragging your soul back in.

Good game, but all multiplayer and online features have been down for months now. From Software refuses to even communicate with their customers to give us any sort of info on whether this will be fixed or not. So we don't know if they are even working on getting it back up and running or not.

This game made me realize that my first souls game was not called Elden ring... It was Zoomer Ring. That being said this game was a lot of fun. I hate poison dart town. Ghosts are stinky. Parries are insanely worth going for. Zoomer ring made me a katana lover so I ran around with a chaos blade, Divine Iaoto and a grass crest shield.
Edit: I forgot to say that as an Elden ring player having jump being tied to running felt weird for a while.

to anyone playing this game for the first time: DON'T go in the graveyard near firelink shrine. Trust me, you don't want to be a sucker like me who picked up this game because everyone said it was really hard, get my ass whooped for an hour then give up on the game for a year because it seemed too hard. Go right, you will see a set of stairs that will eventually lead to undead burg, thats where the real game begins.

tldr.text: Very Positive (92%): players love the gameplay and combat, which 32% of reviews praise.
Bugs and crashes are the most common complaint.

details.text: Recent reviews mention bugs and crashes less often, at 4% against 10% of all reviews.
Newer players are far less positive than veterans, with the longest-time players the most positive of all.
